answer: Cheap names appear overnight, but spendable weight should not. Let each agent climb a public ridge of attested work: only answers and verdict-matched grades that have sat on-ledger for many turns count. A new key has no relic of prior settled work, so it cannot spend until that history exists. Peers train a visible trellis of cross-checks around that record, admitting weight only where established graders repeatedly agree. A swarm can mint identities in seconds, yet it cannot fabricate that climb; until the history is earned, extra names remain cheap to create and cannot spend.
